title: Navigation microflows and access matrix - sidebar prioritization (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a pragmatic set of microflow sketches and an access matrix to guide a redesigned left rail. The aim is to reduce click depth for common tasks, make routing predictable for cross-team flows (SRE, Platform, Product), and encode access affordances in the IA so users only see relevant routes at any time.

Problem statement (quick):
- Console has grown organically; left rail is long and noisy.
- Users can’t reliably find task-specific entry points (e.g., ‘pin model for canary’ vs ‘deploy capacity’).
- Different personas need different primary flows; current nav is flat and role-agnostic.
- Routing fragility: deep links break when we rename pages; route semantics are inconsistent across modules.

Design goals / guardrails:
- Task-first: primary nav should prioritize frequent microflows (deploy, rollout, inspect, troubleshoot) not product nouns.
- Predictable deep links: stable route namespace with fallbacks and canonical redirect rules.
- Minimal discovery cost: compact rail with progressive disclosure (task rail expands to full module view).
- Access-aware: surface only routes user can act on; read-only links visible but de-emphasized.
- Low friction for cross-team handoffs: shareable microflow URLs and ‘jump to’ affordances.

Key terms used in this doc:
- Microflow: the sequence of screens/steps a user takes to complete a discrete task (e.g., create a model route, pin variant).
- Task rail: condensed left rail mode focused on actions.
- Route-wrapping: the rule set that maps legacy URLs to canonical routes and graceful fallbacks.

Microflow sketches (textual wireframes) - prioritized list:
1) Create new deployment (SRE/Platform common) - target <2 clicks from rail:
   - Task rail primary item: 'Deploy' -> modal w/ quick template chooser -> 'Confirm' -> onboarding to rollout wizard page (canonical route /deploy/:id)
   Acceptance: user lands on /deploy/:id and can copy stable link; rollback button visible in header.

2) Canary rollout pin (Product/Dev) - target shallow path:
   - From model page -> quick action 'Pin canary' (small inline overlay) -> modal for traffic split -> commit -> route /models/:id/rollouts/:rid (canonical).
   Acceptance: deep link to /models/:id/rollouts/:rid opens overlay if within model context, otherwise full page with breadcrumb and a subtle CTA to return to model.

3) Troubleshoot trace (SRE/Support) - correlate traces to model requests:
   - Rail item: "Observability" -> Quick search box (request id) -> redirect to /traces/:traceId with time range preserved -> open trace plus side pane with request metadata and link to original route.
   Acceptance: all trace links include model route id param when present.

4) Cost quick-scan (FinOps/Product)
   - Rail item: "Costs" -> compact dashboard -> expand to route-level cost (/costs?route=...) -> suggestion pill to optimize (links to Optimize recommendations).

Routing conventions and rules:
- Canonical routes: every major object (model, deployment, rollout, route, trace) has a canonical path: /models/:id, /deploy/:id, /rollouts/:id, /routes/:id, /traces/:id.
- Legacy aliasing: older patterns (e.g., /model?id=123) must 301/302 to canonical. Front-end should implement silent redirect with a small indicator at top: "Redirected from legacy link".
- Route-wrapping fallback: when a canonical route references a missing resource, attempt to resolve by prefix match (e.g., model name -> id), then show helpful recovery card with links to search.
- Overlay behavior: small tasks should open overlays when user is already on an object context; overlays must map to distinct anchorable URLs so they are shareable.

Sidebar behavior patterns (modes):
- Compact (default for new users): shows 6 top task icons (Deploy, Models, Observability, Costs, Routes, Settings) + hamburger for expand.
- Expanded (power users): full labels, module sections grouped by persona (Platform, Product, SRE, FinOps).
- Contextual: when inside a module (e.g., models), a secondary rail slides in with object-specific actions (Create route, Rollout, Evaluate).
- Sticky quick-actions: a small persistent + button opens a global command palette for cross-module microflows (keyboard-first).

Access matrix (mapping roles -> visible primary routes) - quick table summary (verbal):
- Admins: see everything. Primary rail: Deploy, Models, Observability, Costs, Routes, Settings, Audit.
- Platform Engineer: Deploy, Models, Observability, Routes, Infra, Dedicated Capacity.
- Product Engineer: Models, Rollouts, Observability (read/write), Feature Flags (if connected).
- SRE/Oncall: Observability, Traces, Deploy (read/write limited), Incidents.
- FinOps/Analyst: Costs, Reports, Suggest (Optimize recommendations read-only/writable by Admin).
Notes: access levels must be explicit per-route (view vs act). UI should display read-only affordance (muted actions) rather than hiding entirely for auditability.

Wireframe writeups (page descriptions):
- Models list page (compact): left column filter (tag, runtime, quantization), middle: model cards w/ health & cost micro-metrics, right: quick actions (deploy, evaluate, pin) collapsed into kebab for small screens.
- Deploy wizard (multi-step): top breadcrumb + progress bar, step-specific validation, final page shows stable share link and suggested metrics to monitor.
- Route details: header shows canonical id, owner badge, role-based action row; below: traffic chart, recent traces, pinned prompts (if any), and rollouts history.

Backlog grooming: prioritized tickets (rough):
- HIGH: Implement canonical route mapping middleware + legacy aliases (PROD-412).
- HIGH: Left rail compact mode + task-rail toggle prototype (PROD-421).
- MEDIUM: Overlay URL anchoring pattern for 3 common microflows (pin canary, quick-deploy, copy-trace).
- MEDIUM: Access matrix enforcement for primary rail rendering (feature-flag gated).
- LOW: Cost suggestion pills with direct link to Optimize recommendations.

Open questions / unresolved choices:
- How aggressively do we hide vs de-emphasize routes for restricted roles? (audit visibility tradeoffs)
- Should overlays be implemented as separate routes or client-state-only modals? Pref leaning to routes for shareability.
- Do we surface error states for legacy redirects or silently auto-resolve?

Next steps / action items:
- Design: iterate compact rail visuals, propose 3 icon sets and a 2-level animation spec (Priya) - due 2025-01-24.
- Engineering: spike canonical route middleware and alias map (Rafael) - evaluate infra impacts and caching.
- PM: finalize role definitions for access matrix and produce feature flag plan (Maya) - due 2025-01-30.
- UX Research: run 5 moderated sessions focusing on "deploy" and "pin canary" microflows to validate 2-click targets (Ethan) - recruit by 2025-01-20.

Notes to reviewer: this is intentionally pragmatic — we want to ship a compact-task-first rail quickly and iterate on personalization later. Please add comments inline in the Linear task linked above and flag any unaccounted persona flows.

Related links and artifacts (quick paste):
- Existing IA map: confluence:Console-IA-v3 (for reference)
- Linear epic: https://linear.app/RFO/PROD-400/console-navigation-redesign
- Slack thread w/ initial sketches: https://slack.redwood/#console-ux-427

TL;DR: Move from a flat, noun-based left rail to a compact, task-first rail with stable canonical routes and overlay URLs. Pair with an explicit access matrix so users only see actions they can take and deep links become predictable and shareable.
